security_audit.summary: All 48 static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, fixed command substitution, or intentional Git worktree paths. Semantic review found real operational risks from destructive resets, remote history rewriting, and test execution across historical revisions. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: Hard reset examples can discard uncommitted work.
remediation.suggestion: Require a clean status check, explicit user confirmation, and a backup branch before every hard reset.

remediation.issue: Automated bisect examples execute scripts from historical revisions.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to inspect scripts first and run historical code in an isolated environment without secrets or network credentials.

remediation.issue: Force-with-lease examples still rewrite remote history.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation that the branch is private, freshly fetched, and not protected before any force push.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Git Reset Guidance
semantic_findings.description: Executable hard reset examples can irreversibly discard uncommitted files and index changes without requiring a clean status check or explicit confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Each cited line directly invokes git reset --hard. The surrounding guidance does not consistently require preflight checks or confirmation.

semantic_findings.title: Historical Code Execution During Automated Bisect
semantic_findings.description: Automated bisect runs repository scripts across historical revisions, which may execute untrusted code with the current user's credentials and network access.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both cited commands instruct Git to execute project test commands repeatedly after checking out historical commits. No isolation or script-review warning is provided.

semantic_findings.title: Remote History Rewrite Without Required Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: Force-with-lease examples can rewrite a remote branch and disrupt collaborators, although the skill includes partial safety guidance.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands explicitly perform force pushes. Force-with-lease reduces accidental overwrites but does not remove the remote history rewrite.

content.value_statement: Advanced Git work can rewrite history, lose changes, or disrupt shared branches. This skill provides structured workflows, safety checks, and recovery steps for complex repository tasks.
actual_capabilities: Explains interactive rebase actions for reordering, combining, editing, or dropping commits.
Guides single, ranged, and staged cherry-pick workflows across branches.
Uses manual or automated Git bisect workflows to identify a regression commit.
Organizes parallel branch development with Git worktrees and cleanup steps.
Shows reflog-based recovery for deleted branches, lost commits, and mistaken resets.
Compares rebase and merge strategies for local, shared, and release branches.
limitations: It provides guidance but cannot guarantee repository state, permissions, or remote branch policies.
Referenced supporting files and scripts are not included in this package.
Examples use placeholder branches, commits, paths, versions, and test commands.
Destructive commands require independent review, backups, and explicit confirmation.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Reviewable Feature Branch
use_cases.description: Create a safe plan to squash fixups, reorder commits, and update a pull request without overwriting collaborators.
use_cases.target_user: Software developer preparing a pull request

use_cases.title: Trace a Regression
use_cases.description: Plan a manual or isolated automated bisect between known good and bad revisions.
use_cases.target_user: Release engineer investigating a production regression

use_cases.title: Recover Repository Work
use_cases.description: Use reflog evidence to restore commits or branches after a mistaken reset, deletion, or history edit.
use_cases.target_user: Team lead assisting with repository recovery

prompt_templates.title: Inspect My Branch Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current Git branch state and explain safe next steps. Start with read-only checks and do not change files or history.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review before an advanced Git operation

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Clean Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan how to clean commits on [feature branch] before merging into [base branch]. Identify shared commits and request confirmation before rewriting history.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Regression Bisect
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a bisect between [good revision] and [bad revision]. Explain the test signal and isolate any historical scripts before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Recover From a Git Mistake
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this reflog and repository status: [details]. Propose the least destructive recovery, preserve current work, and include verification and rollback steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced recovery after reset, rebase, or branch deletion

output_examples.input: I have five local commits with two fixups. Help me prepare a clean pull request.
output: Confirm that the branch is private and create a backup reference.
Review the commit order and identify each fixup target.
Use an interactive autosquash plan, run tests, and inspect the final comparison.
Request confirmation before updating the remote branch.

output_examples.input: A regression appeared after version 2.1. Plan a safe bisect.
output: Verify one known good revision and one reproducibly bad revision.
Define a deterministic pass or fail test.
Inspect historical test scripts and use an isolated environment before automation.
Reset the bisect state after recording the first bad commit.

output_examples.input: I deleted a branch and need its last commit.
output_examples.output: Inspect the reflog without changing repository state, locate the branch tip, create a recovery branch, and verify its contents before cleanup.

best_practices: Inspect status, recent history, remotes, and branch sharing before changing commits.
Create a backup reference and define rollback steps before destructive or history-rewriting operations.
Run tests and compare the resulting branch against its base before pushing.
anti_patterns: Do not rebase or force push a shared branch without explicit coordination.
Do not run historical repository scripts with secrets, broad permissions, or unrestricted network access.
Do not use hard reset until current changes are reviewed, preserved, or intentionally discarded.

faq.question: Can this skill run Git commands automatically?
faq.answer: It supplies workflow guidance and command examples. Execution depends on the host agent, available tools, repository permissions, and user approval.

faq.question: Does it support interactive rebase?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains picking, rewording, editing, squashing, fixing up, dropping, reordering, and splitting commits.

faq.question: Can it recover deleted commits or branches?
faq.answer: It explains reflog-based recovery while the relevant reflog entries remain available.

faq.question: Is force-with-lease always safe?
faq.answer: No. It reduces accidental overwrites but still rewrites remote history and requires branch ownership, a fresh fetch, and team coordination.

faq.question: Can it diagnose regressions?
faq.answer: Yes. It outlines manual and automated bisect workflows using known good and bad revisions.

faq.question: Are the referenced resources included?
faq.answer: No. This package contains only SKILL.md, so referenced guides, assets, and scripts are unavailable.
